entries.name: Biological applications of bifurcation theory
entries.definition: The use of bifurcation theory, which studies how the behaviour of a dynamical system changes qualitatively as its parameters vary, to model biological systems.

entries.name: Biomedical informatics
entries.definition: The field that applies information science and computing to the collection, storage and analysis of biological and medical data.

entries.name: Biomolecular engineering
entries.definition: Engineering that designs and modifies biological molecules such as proteins and nucleic acids for use in medicine, industry and research.

entries.name: Biopesticide
entries.definition: Pest-control agents made from natural materials such as microbes, plants and minerals.

entries.name: Biopython
entries.definition: An open-source Python library of tools for computational biology and bioinformatics, such as reading sequence files and working with protein structures.

entries.name: Biosensors
entries.definition: Devices that pair a biological recognition element, such as an enzyme or antibody, with a transducer to detect a specific substance.

entries.name: Bioterrorism preparedness and response
entries.definition: Planning for, detecting and responding to the deliberate release of biological agents that cause disease.

entries.name: Bismuth sulfite agar
entries.definition: A selective culture medium used in microbiology to isolate Salmonella, especially Salmonella Typhi, from samples.

entries.name: Bitly
entries.definition: A link-management platform that shortens web addresses and tracks how the short links are used.

entries.name: BlackLine
entries.definition: A cloud platform for automating financial close tasks such as account reconciliation and transaction matching.

entries.name: Blast radius analysis
entries.definition: Assessing the bounded scope and impact of a failure or action.

entries.name: Blended learning
entries.definition: A teaching approach that combines online digital media with traditional face-to-face classroom instruction.

entries.name: Blender Game Engine
entries.definition: The built-in real-time 3D game and interactive-content engine that shipped with Blender until version 2.80.

entries.name: Boa Constructor
entries.definition: A cross-platform integrated development environment and GUI builder for Python and wxPython, written in Python.

entries.name: Board support package
entries.definition: Developing the low-level code and drivers that let an operating system run on a specific hardware board.

entries.name: Body contouring
entries.definition: Performing cosmetic procedures that reduce fat or tighten and reshape areas of the body.

entries.name: BODYATTACK
entries.definition: A Les Mills group fitness class of high-energy athletic moves such as running and jumping, set to music.

entries.name: BODYPUMP
entries.definition: A Les Mills group fitness class of barbell strength training with many repetitions, set to music.

entries.name: Boiler draft
entries.definition: The pressure difference that moves combustion air and flue gases through a boiler furnace and stack.

entries.name: Bonjour
entries.definition: Apple's implementation of zero-configuration networking, which lets devices and services on a local network find each other automatically.

entries.name: Boolean algebra
entries.definition: The branch of algebra in which variables take the values true or false and are combined with operations such as AND, OR and NOT.

entries.name: Boolean search
entries.definition: Searching by combining terms with operators such as AND, OR and NOT, as in recruiting and research databases.

entries.name: Border studies
entries.definition: An interdisciplinary field that studies political borders and boundaries and how they shape people, places and states.

entries.name: Box API
entries.definition: The programming interface of the Box cloud content-management service, used to manage files, folders, users and permissions from other software.

entries.name: Box Backup
entries.definition: An open-source automatic online backup system with a client and a server.

entries.name: Brand communication
entries.definition: Conveying a brand's identity, message and values to its audiences through consistent channels and content.

entries.name: Brand strategy
entries.definition: Defining a brand's long-term purpose, audience, positioning and identity so that its choices stay consistent.

entries.name: Brand positioning
entries.definition: Defining and defending a brand promise for an audience.

entries.name: Branding
entries.definition: Creating and managing the name, identity and reputation by which a product, organisation or person is recognised.

entries.name: Breast surgery
entries.definition: Surgical operations on the breast, such as lumpectomy, mastectomy, reconstruction and augmentation.

entries.name: Breeze.js
entries.definition: A JavaScript library for managing data in rich client applications, with querying, caching and change tracking against a server.

entries.name: Bridal consulting
entries.definition: Advising engaged couples, especially brides, on choosing wedding gowns and accessories or on planning the wedding.

entries.name: Brightway
entries.definition: An open-source Python framework for life cycle assessment, used to model the environmental impacts of products and processes.

entries.name: Broadcast programming
entries.definition: Selecting and scheduling the shows and other content that a television or radio station or network broadcasts.

entries.name: Browzwear
entries.definition: 3D fashion design software for creating and simulating garments digitally before they are made.

entries.name: Brute-force search
entries.definition: Solving a problem by systematically trying every possible candidate solution until one works.

entries.name: Btrieve
entries.definition: A record-oriented database engine, originally from Pervasive Software, that stores and retrieves records through key indexes.

entries.name: Budtending
entries.definition: Advising customers on and selling cannabis products in a dispensary.

entries.name: Bug tracking systems
entries.definition: Software used to record, prioritise and follow software defects until they are fixed.

entries.name: Builder's risk insurance
entries.definition: Insurance that covers a building and its materials against damage while it is under construction or renovation.
